verses.text: Hannah prayed, “My heart celebrates in the LORD! The LORD has lifted my horn in triumph. I can speak boldly over my enemies because I rejoice in how you've rescued me.
Nobody is holy like the LORD. There is no one besides you, and no rock like our God.
Stop talking so proudly. Don't let arrogance come out of your mouth. The LORD knows everything, and he weighs what people do.
The bows of the mighty are broken, and those who stumbled are clothed with strength.

People who had plenty now work for a piece of bread, while those who went hungry have enough. The woman who couldn't have children has given birth to seven, while the woman with many children is wasting away.
The LORD takes life and gives life. He brings people down to Sheol and raises them up.
The LORD makes people poor or rich. He brings people low, and he lifts them up.

He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the garbage heap. He seats them with princes and gives them a place of honor. The pillars of the earth belong to the LORD. He set the world on them.
He'll guard the steps of his faithful ones, but the wicked will be silenced in darkness. Nobody wins by strength alone.

Those who fight the LORD will be shattered. He'll thunder against them from heaven. The LORD will judge to the ends of the earth. He'll give strength to his king and raise up the horn of his anointed one.”
Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy stayed and served the LORD under Eli the priest.
Eli's sons were wicked men who didn't know the LORD.
Here's how the priests treated people. Whenever someone brought a sacrifice, the priest's servant arrived while the meat was boiling, carrying a three-pronged fork.
He stuck the fork into the pan, kettle, cauldron, or pot, and the priest kept whatever came up on it. They did this to every Israelite who came to Shiloh.
Even before the fat was burned, the priest's servant would tell the person offering the sacrifice, “Give the priest meat to roast. He wants it raw. He won't take boiled meat.”
If the person said, “Burn the fat first, and then take as much as you want,” the servant would answer, “Give it to me now, or I'll take it by force.”
The young men's sin was very serious in the LORD's sight because they treated his offering with contempt.
Meanwhile Samuel served before the LORD. He was still a boy and wore a linen ephod.
Each year his mother made him a little robe and brought it when she came with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, “May the LORD give you children through this woman in place of the child she asked for and gave to the LORD.” Then they went home.
The LORD cared for Hannah. She became pregnant and had three sons and two daughters. Samuel grew up in the LORD's presence.
By then Eli was very old. He heard how his sons were treating all Israel and how they slept with the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
He asked them, “Why are you doing these things? I'm hearing about your evil behavior from everyone.
This has to stop, my sons. What I'm hearing is terrible. You're leading the LORD's people into disobedience.

If someone sins against another person, God can judge between them. But if someone sins against the LORD, who can plead for them?” They didn't listen to their father, because the LORD intended to put them to death.
Samuel kept growing and found more favor with both the LORD and the people.
A man of God came to Eli and said, “The LORD says, ‘Didn't I reveal myself to your ancestor's family when they were enslaved by Pharaoh in Egypt?

Didn't I choose your ancestor from all of Israel's tribes to be my priest, to go up to my altar, burn incense, and wear an ephod before me? Didn't I give his household all the Israelites' offerings made by fire?

Why do you treat the sacrifices and offerings I commanded for my dwelling with contempt? Why do you honor your sons above me and fatten yourselves on the best of every offering from my people Israel?’

So the LORD, the God of Israel, says, ‘I did promise that your family and your ancestor's family would serve before me forever.’ But now the LORD says, ‘Far be that from me. I'll honor those who honor me, and those who despise me will be cursed.
The time is coming when I'll cut short your strength and the strength of your ancestral family, so no man in your household will live to old age.
You'll see trouble in my dwelling, even while I give Israel good things in abundance. There will never be an old man in your household.
Anyone I leave serving at my altar will wear out your eyes with tears and bring grief to your heart. Your descendants will die in the prime of their lives.
What happens to your sons Hophni and Phinehas will be your sign. They'll both die on the same day.
I'll raise up a faithful priest who will do what's in my heart and mind. I'll give him a family that endures, and he'll serve before my anointed one forever.
Everyone left in your household will come and bow before him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread. They'll say, “Please give me one of the priests' duties so I can have a bite to eat.”’”
